newsitem.title: USA: S&P revises capital adequacy model for insurers.
newsitem.headline: S&P revises capital adequacy model for insurers.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Tuesday that it was revising its capital adequacy model for the investment portfolios of life and health insurance companies.
Among the changes, S&P will revise the credit risk charges for commercial and agricultural mortgage investments and streamline its system for assessing risk charges on group major medical business.
It will also change its treatment of single-issuer concentration in excess of 10 percent to 15 percent of total risk-adjusted capital.

"This may have an effect on ratings of certain companies, but there are no way to predict in advance the type of company that would be most affected," said Jack Reichman, associate director in S&P's insurance rating group.
The changes will take effect by the end of 1996, S&P said.
Few Wall Street analysts felt the revisions would have much of an impact on insurance company ratings, although most were only vaguely familiar with the changes to the model.
